Dear Family:
I left Shanghai on Saturday, July 3, for an inspection
trip to Canton, Hong Kong, and Macao
with the new Managing Director
of CNAC, Colonel Lum Wei Shing. The Colonel was formerly a General
but along with dozens of others in the Chinese army, was reduced
in rank two years ago when the Chinese army was reorganized, and
they tried to give the title ot General more significance than that
of Colonel in Kentucky. There are still plenty of generals and the
title continues to carry so little distinction that the real Number
Ones usually affect some more face-giving rank such as Field Mar-
shal, Air Mershal, and of course the topside Number One is
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-Shek.
We flew to Canton on Saturday and
spent July 4th there.
It was
terribly hot and I was glad to go
out to the International Club in the country for lunch.
There we
met several of the American pilots from Hangchon who had flown
down to Canton also on an inspection trip with General Wong, head
of the Chinese Air Force. Most of the Chinese top men in aviation
are graduates of american aviation schools and of course all speak
English. Spending the Fourth of July in Canton reminded me that
just four years ago we made the first commercial flight from Shanghai
down the coast. Un that occasion we also left Shanghai on July 3,
but spent the night at Foochow and continued our trip on the fol-
lowing day.
On board our ship, four years ago, we had a German-
American,
Paul Groeger.
a good sport and lots of fun, but
sometimes a bit slow on the trigger. As we went in for a landing
at amoy,
all ships in the harbor
were "dressed" and all of course
flying American flags in recognition of our independence day.. I
called out to Groeger who sat across
the aisle from me, "Pretty
nice of them to give us this welcome"! Groeger smiled
and nodded.
I think he secretly felt that we fully deserved the recognition.
The rest of the day he went around stepping high with his chest well
out and a bit of swagger.
Finally he thanked someone for the wel-
come and discovered his error. A few minutes later, he came around
to me and said "Deese flags and decorations are not for us. Dis is
George Washington's birthday"!
Well to return to my story--in Canton there were no flags
and no firecrackers, it was just the fourth day of the seventh moon.

conditioned car, very popular this time of the year. It was a
